articleTitle: AI Engineering Continuum: Concept and Expected Foundation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: To address the breadth of AI quality risks including security ones, we propose the “AI Engineering Continuum” as a comprehensive framework consisting of the following five dimensions necessary from the holistic engineering point of view: AI layer continuum, AI process continuum, AI computing continuum, AI automation continuum, and AI quality continuum. The AI engineering continuum is intended to be used to evaluate the adequacy of AI engineering projects and identify weaknesses that should be improved and aligned with the dimensions of the framework. Furthermore, we discuss necessary engineering features and foundations needed to efficiently and effectively raise each dimension of the framework and demonstrate some of their preliminary implementations, including our past achievements.

Author Keywords: Software Engineering for AI and Machine Learning

articleTitle: Anchored Input-Output Encoding for Improving the Performance of Temporal Convolutional Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Exploiting Deep Learning models for time series modeling and forecasting is a very promising approach given the learning capabilities of such large neural models. The Sample Convolution and Interaction Network (SCINet) has been an established Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) for time series modeling using standard inputs. Using sophisticated input and output encoding with anchors for improving robustness and accuracy has been proposed as a promising alternative in the anchored Input-Output (AnIO) Learning method. In this work, we propose a new model for electric load demand forecasting which is a time series modelling problem by introducing the AnIO-SCINet hybrid model that exploits the strengths of both approaches. The experimental results show an improvement in performance and accuracy over the standard SCINet on predicting the electric load demand for the Greek Energy Market.

articleTitle: A Methodology for Collecting, Processing and Validating Team Members' Contribution Data in the Academic Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Appraising team members' contribution to common team tasks is a difficult task since individual work is often covered by team functions. In this study we argue that appraisal of team fellows' contribution by their peers within a team is proven as a well objective measure. Peer ranking of the contribution of each team member was used to form a Peer Contribution Score which was normalized for number of team tasks for which appraisal has been received and for number of team members provided rankings. This was compared to and validated by the external observation leveling of each team member's performance by the research team. We verified that Peer Contribution Score was in line with the external observed level of team members' performance. Whereas this work was carried out in the academic environment focusing student teams, extension to business environment could be possible and seems attractive to be attempted.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Cloud Continuum Computing Resources: A Mathematical Programming Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) and advancements in cloud and fog computing have catalyzed the development of the Cloud Continuum, an enhanced cloud system integrating diverse computational resources and services. This paper introduces the Cloud Fog Service Broker (CFSB) designed to facilitate the evaluation and selection of these resources within the cloud continuum ecosystem. The CFSB employs Multiple-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) methods that rely on Mathematical Programming to assess resources based on multiple factors. This integration allows for a comprehensive assessment, ranking resources by synthesizing these diverse criteria and incorporating user preferences through weight restrictions in optimization models. The architecture, criteria, evaluation process and an illustrative example of the CFSB's application highlight its role in decision-making for cloud resource selection.

articleTitle: GRoup AFFEct Recognition: The Side of Heartbeats
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: This paper extends our ongoing research series on GRAFFER (GRoup AFFEct Recognition) and specifically focuses on the analysis of heart rate variations during various events. We examine heart rate data from diverse individuals to identify distinct patterns associated with emotional fluctuations. Our primary aim is to unveil the subtle nuances within heart rate patterns that serve as indicators of distinct emotional fluctuations. Through meticulous comparative analyses, we strive to pinpoint both the shared and distinct signatures linked to varying emotional states. These discoveries are expected to significantly bolster the precision of group emotion detection for participants participating in diverse events, especially those attending remotely. While current versions of GRAFFER are based on facial group samples, our new research approach aims at creating a multi-modal system integrating heart rate data as well as other modalities.

articleTitle: Monitoring of Flow Rate Measurements Using LSTM Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Integration of automation in operation and maintenance (O&M) tasks can enhance early detection of faults in advanced reactors (AR). Data-driven machine learning (ML) methods provide a viable solution for efficiently monitoring equipment in such systems. We use a long short-term memory (LSTM) autoencoder to monitor flow rate measurements in a water pump using multiple features, including flow and pressure measurements. Results show that the prediction error increases as less correlated features are introduced in the model. Moreover, prediction error slightly increases with lookback window length.

articleTitle: Applying LSTM for River's Water Level Forecasting as Potential Flood Indication: A Case Study in Greece
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Floods can have significant life-threatening and economic impacts on human societies. Flood forecasting with data-driven methods is a crucial aspect of disaster risk management, providing valuable insights into potential flood events and allowing for timely mitigation measures. This work illustrates the application of a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network for short-term forecasting of a river's water level. The water treatment data used for training the LSTM models were gathered from Sperchios river, located in central Greece. Historical time-series data in a half-hour interval of the river's water level, water velocity, and area precipitation were utilized for the development of the proposed scheme. The developed model is deployed in the backend of a web application for half-hour ahead predictions of the river's water level that are visualized in the frontend. The post-analysis of the deployed forecasting model indicates that it consistently delivers forecasts with minimal error and demonstrates high accuracy in recent flood events.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cardiac AI Explainability Through Ontology-Based Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: The increasing utilization of Deep Learning models in healthcare and cardiology necessitates robust explainability to ensure trust, understandability and bias mitigation. Especially in cardiology, where life-critical decisions should be made, explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) solutions play a pivotal role. As of now, the utility of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) advancements in explainable AI is limited by the complexity of the explanations provided and the lack of applicability of explanations in real-world clinical settings. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel ontology-based methodology to evaluate XAI techniques, focusing on cardiac “black-box” models. More specifically, we use ontologies to assess and ensure the clarity and relevance of AI explanations, fostering the development of explainable and trustworthy systems for clinical use. Our solution unfolds in sequential phases, beginning with rigorous data preprocessing, feature engineering and continuing with model architecture design and implementation. The next stage includes the deployment of various XAI methods to produce meaningful explanations, which being evaluated by leveraging an ontology scheme.

articleTitle: Implementing a Robust and Scalable Detect-and-Avoid Algorithm for UAV Navigation in ROS
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have garnered significant attention from the research community during the last decade, due to their diverse capabilities and potential applications. One of the most critical functions that drones must execute efficiently is navigation in real-world environments. This paper presents a decentralized approach for enabling unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to navigate safely in unknown environments and avoid obstacles. Leveraging the Optimal Reciprocal Collision Avoidance (ORCA) algorithm, implemented in the Robot Operating System (ROS), our method facilitates conflict detection and resolution in 2D environments. Through simulations using ROS, Gazebo, and Iris drones, we validate the effectiveness of our approach in scenarios with initial trajectory conflicts. Our work addresses the pressing need for UAVs to autonomously plan and execute safe flights, laying the groundwork for enhanced UAV capabilities in various real-world applications. The simulation results demonstrate the efficiency and robustness of our approach.

articleTitle: Impact of Consequenses on Human Trust Dynamics in Artificial Intelligence Responses
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: This paper examines the impact of varying consequences on human trust in AI responses, focusing on how different trust states—trust, mistrust, overtrust, and AI phobia—are affected by three scenarios: Possibly Positive Consequences (+1), Neutral Consequences (0), and Possibly Negative Consequences (−1). In the Possibly Positive Consequences (+1) scenario, where any AI response is better than none due to the inherent chance of success, trust can be upgraded to a higher state if the AI response is reliable. However, mistrust or overtrust may develop if the response is untrustworthy, prompting a reassessment of AI reliance. In the Neutral Consequences (0) scenario, where accepting the AI response poses no negative consequences, the trust state remains unaffected. Trust can be easily established and maintained if the AI response is trustworthy, as the absence of adverse outcomes encourages confidence. Mistrust is mitigated in this scenario due to the lack of perceived downside. However, overtrust can become a concern if individuals rely on AI without critical evaluation, potentially leading to future vulnerabilities. In the Possibly Negative Consequences (−1) scenario, where accepting a potentially erroneous AI response could lead to significant negative outcomes, trust is highly contingent on the AI's accuracy and reliability and therefore trust can easily be down graded to lower levels (mistrust of AI phobia). Even minor errors can lead to a rapid erosion of trust and the establishment of mistrust, diminishing the trust state to a lower level. Overtrust is less likely due to the high stakes involved, but if it does occur, it can lead to severe repercussions.

articleTitle: Intelligent Smoothing and Cumulative Sum Control Methods Applied to Signal Peak Detection in Gamma-Ray Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: The accurate identification of locations containing nuclear materials is of paramount importance for societal safety. Consequently, data analytics techniques can be leveraged to analyze signals and detect potential nuclear threats. In this study, two algorithms are proposed: the first employs a smoothing technique, while the second utilizes cumulative sum control (CUSUM). These methods are evaluated using five sets of real-world gamma measurements containing artificially introduced spectral peaks of different magnitudes and positions. On average, the intelligent smoothing approach correctly identified 66.6% of the peaks, while the cumulative sum control method achieved an identification rate of 83.4% for the peaks.

articleTitle: Benchmarking of Machine Learning Algorithms for Temperature Sensor Fault Time Series Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Reliable sensors functioning is important for safe and efficient operation of a nuclear system. Accurate detection and classification of sensor anomalies are crucial for efficient maintenance and prevention of reactor shutdowns. In this proof-of-principle study, we benchmark performance of several machine learning (ML) algorithms in temperature sensor fault detection. The database consists of four time series, with one representing normal sensor operation and the remaining three consisting of various sensor faults. The ML models in this study include Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, Decision Tree (DT), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). Performance of the ML models is evaluated using Precision, Recall and F1-score metrics. The results of the benchmarking study show that XGBoost achieves the best performance.

articleTitle: Mathematical Representation of Memory and Schema for Improving Human-Generative AI Interactions
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: In this paper, we explore memory and Schema through the lens of mathematical representation. This approach aims to define more abstract themes about cognitive processes, to simulate and enhance interactions between Generative AI systems and humans. By doing so, humans can leverage their experiences and interactions in ways that improve the performance and personalization of the large language models they interact with. Furthermore, by formalizing these concepts using set theory, we can increase performance and base the accuracy of responses on streamlined historical conversations. This involves organizing data into logical clusters (memory) that utilize information (Schema) in a more comprehensive and structured manner. We define memory as a function of time and size, where the size of memory decays as time passes. The resolution of memory also fades, leading us to add more abstraction to our memory function. Memories with thematic resemblance are then structured into Schemas based on a maturity threshold influenced by criticality, emotional-user interaction, and mass, which is the measure of the summation of related memories.

articleTitle: Mentoring Mastery: Methodological Strategies for Adult Trainer Empowerment in DigComp Framework Application
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: This paper outlines the methodological approach in a mentoring program designed to help adult trainers effectively employ the DigComp Framework in designing, creating, and assessing adult learning programs. As the second phase of a two-step training sequence, this mentoring program offers customized guidance and support, enabling trainers to integrate DigComp principles into their educational strategies. The paper details the mentoring schema, organizational procedures, methodological steps, and comprehensive data collection methods developed to evaluate the program's effectiveness. Initial findings are shared, highlighting the method's success in facilitating adult trainers' understanding of the DigComp Framework. This study contributes valuable insights into the practical use of the DigComp Framework in adult education settings and suggests directions for future research and development of training programs.

articleTitle: Applicability Filtering Model for S1000D Documents Using AND/OR Trees
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Technical documentation written using the S1000D norm in aeronautics and aerospace fields is based on ‘applicability’ tags that define the context in which a document or part of it is valid. Filtering data modules by applicability is challenging because tags can have the potential to accumulate infinitely, reaching a level of complexity that becomes challenging for human interpretation. On the other hand, many changes were made to the applicability tag's structure when upgraded from version 2.3 to version 4.1. This paper presents a general AND/OR tree-based model to filter documents based on their applicability. Transformations were made to both versions to get a unique one, thereby, evaluating the input values and selecting accessible content for each user. The model has shown accurate filtering for all tests made, on multiple datasets of different versions, having applicability of different complexity ranges.

articleTitle: AI-Based Models for Predicting the Risk of Developing Diabetes
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Diabetes is a serious condition affecting hundreds of millions of people worldwide. Diabetic risk prediction is an important task and preliminary risk assessments are crucial for clinicians for achieving prioritization of diabetes cases and for examining cases with higher risk first In this work we collect and analyse podiatry data related to diabetes prediction and develop and evaluate Machine Learning models using the created dataset for providing preliminary assessments of diabetes risk and help clinicians on the task of prioritizing cases according to the predicted risk.

articleTitle: Predictive Vigilance: Harnessing Internet of Things and Machine Learning for Smoke Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: The increasing prevalence of fire incidents in various environments underscores the critical need for advanced smoke detection systems. This paper presents a novel approach, termed “Predictive Vigilance”, which integrates Internet of Things (IoT) sensors with state-of-the-art machine learning techniques to enhance smoke detection capabilities. By leveraging the inter-connectedness of IoT devices and the computational power of machine learning algorithms, a system can achieve real-time monitoring and predictive analysis of smoke presence. We propose a framework that combines sensor data acquisition, preprocessing, feature extraction, and classification using machine learning models. Through extensive experimentation and validation, we demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our approach in detecting smoke accurately while minimizing false alarms. Furthermore, we discuss potential applications and implications of Predictive Vigilance in diverse settings, including residential, commercial, and industrial environments. Overall, this paper contributes to the advancement of proactive fire safety measures by harnessing the synergy between IoT technology and machine learning for smoke detection.

articleTitle: Real-Time Monitoring for an IoT-Based Aquatic Microecosystem
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Maintaining optimal water quality is not only crucial for human health but also for the well-being of marine life. In biomedical research, the use of fish has become increasingly prevalent due to their importance in studying biological processes and human diseases. However, manual maintenance of fish tanks in laboratories often leads to errors that can adversely affect research outcomes and the health of the fish. This paper proposes the solution of an automated mini aquarium designed to provide an optimal living environment for any species of fish, without the need for human intervention. This low-cost, low-consumption solution is equipped with a self-regulating system and sensors that monitor parameters such as pH, temperature, turbidity, Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) values and the level of the water. These features work synergistically to monitor the conditions of the microecosystem, reducing the room for error and the need for manual labor. The Internet of Things (IoT) technology will be critical for an unsupervised fully functioning and safe aquarium, making it accessible for every laboratory, scientist and hobbyist. The long-term benefits of this solution include improved research outcomes and increased longevity of the fish.

articleTitle: A Multi-Layer Perceptron Neural Network-based Access Control Mechanism to Breast Cancer Patients' Health Data
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: In recent decades the risk of cancer has increased due to the modern lifestyle. A common type of these cases is breast cancer. Breast cancer is a disease in which breast cells grow out of control. Usually, if not detected in time, breast cancer spreads to other parts of the body, with usually an irreversible result. Nowadays, artificial intelligence provides substantial assistance to medical personnel in examining the possibility of the development of cancerous tumors. This research focuses on examining the characteristics of various tumors that appear and classifying them as either benign or malignant through machine learning techniques. In our research, we developed an algorithm for predicting a possible related health problem, which is based on the technology of Deep Neural Networks, and which examines data characteristics of a given volume whose benignity or malignancy is being investigated. At the same time, the optimal design of the architectural features of the Neural Network is being studied. Finally, this machine learning mechanism is integrated in our access control system of patients' medical health information, as studied in several of our previous works, so as to enrich this medical system and to safeguard the patients' wellbeing, their medical data security, and to inform the doctor about the patient's medical situation.

articleTitle: Reliability of CNN-Based No-Reference Video Quality Metrics
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: As the multimedia contents have been increasingly delivered over networks, quality monitoring has become an important issue. Although full-reference (FR) and reduced-reference (RR) methods for objective video quality measurements have been successfully developed and adapted as international standards, no-reference (NR) methods have failed to produce satisfactory performance. However, recently deep-learning based NR methods have shown promising results. In particular, when test video sets are different from training video sets, it is observed that the performance can be substantially lower. Also, they still have a reliability problem. In this paper, we explore the reasoning reliability of deep-learning based NR methods with various experiments.

articleTitle: Infrared Computer Vision for Utility-Scale Photovoltaic Array Inspection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Utility-scale solar arrays require specialized inspection methods for detecting faulty panels. Photovoltaic (PV) panel faults caused by weather, ground leakage, circuit issues, temperature, environment, age, and other damage can take many forms but often symptomatically exhibit temperature differences. Included is a mini survey to review these common faults and PV array fault detection approaches. Among these, infrared thermography cameras are a powerful tool for improving solar panel inspection in the field. These can be combined with other technologies, including image processing and machine learning. This position paper examines several computer vision algorithms that automate thermal anomaly detection in infrared imagery. We demonstrate our infrared thermography data collection approach, the PV thermal imagery benchmark dataset, and the measured performance of image processing transformations, including the Hough Transform for PV segmentation. The results of this implementation are presented with a discussion of future work.

articleTitle: Spot Price Prediction in Electricity Markets Using an Ensemble of Extreme Learning Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: The electricity spot price, the wholesale cost paid by utility companies, has experienced increased volatility due to the need for equilibrium between supply and demand. Traditional spot price models have been explored to project electricity demand for the next day, but the emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has sparked interest in using this tool for spot pricing, given its robust data modeling capabilities. However, AI modeling often demands extensive data processing or significant computational power, prompting the exploration of Extreme Learning Machines (ELMs) as an alternative. ELMs have gained popularity for their ability to generalize data effectively without extensive computational requirements. In this study, we propose employing an ensemble of ELM models to forecast the average next day-ahead electricity spot price. Real day-ahead electricity spot prices from the European Network of Transmission System Operators for Electricity (ENTSO-E) were used to evaluate the performance of the ensemble ELM. Our findings indicate that the ensemble ELM performs comparably to larger, more complex traditional models but with significantly reduced computation time.

articleTitle: An Incremental Learning Assurance Approach for Intent Based Networking Enabled Data Centers
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Intent Based Networking (IBN) is a novel paradigm that aims to create a closed-loop automation towards building a self-governed network. An inherent part of IBN is the network assurance, which tries to automatically detect any performance drift and propose a remedy solution. Following this trend, in this paper we propose a novel IBN -enabled network assurance approach in a data center setting, in order to predict key resource utilization metrics and to help network administrators to proactively take corrective actions when needed. Specifically, we propose an incremental learning approach for data center assurance, designed to accommodate the dynamic nature of infrastructures. Experimental findings obtained from real-world datasets substantiate the effectiveness of our approach, demonstrating its ability to accurately forecast resource utilization even amidst highly dynamic environments.

articleTitle: LYRICEL: A Rule-Augmented Artificial Intelligence-Empowered Cultural E-Learning with GPT and Machine Learning for Song Lyrics
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: In this paper, we present LYRICEL, an advanced AI-enhanced system that combines a rule-based decision-making mechanism, OpenAI's application programming interface (API), and additional external machine learning and analytical APIs to deliver song lyrics recommendations for an e-learning platform dedicated to Greek music and songs. This new component enhances MUSILYAN, a specialised software tool designed for musicological and lyrical analysis, by complementing it with GPT4o's capabilities. While ChatGPT excels in natural language understanding and generation, MUSILYAN provides structured semantic content management and thematic organization of lyrics. The integration of the two modules in LYRICEL, holds significant promise for enhancing the exploration and understanding of poetry and lyrics, offering a robust framework for enriching cultural heritage e-learning experiences.

articleTitle: Enhancing Predictive Maintenance with Interpretable AutoML: A Case Study on Detecting Ball-Bearing Faults Using IoT Data
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Predictive maintenance has emerged as a crucial approach to enhance the reliability and efficiency of industrial systems. Leveraging Internet of Things (IoT) data, predictive maintenance enables the timely detection and prevention of equipment failures, thereby minimizing downtime and maintenance costs. In this paper, we present a framework for predictive maintenance using interpretable machine learning algorithms, facilitated by Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) techniques. Focusing specifically on ball-bearing faults, a common issue in many mechanical systems, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach in accurately predicting impending failures.

articleTitle: Enhancing Occupancy Detection Through IoT: A Comparative Analysis of Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive comparative analysis of classifier performance for enhancing occupancy detection in Internet of Things (IoT) environments. Occupancy detection is a crucial aspect in various applications such as smart buildings, energy management, and security systems. Leveraging IoT data, we evaluate the effectiveness of different classifiers in accurately detecting occupancy. Through experimentation and analysis, we identify the strengths and limitations of various classifiers, providing insights into their suitability for real-world deployment. Our findings offer valuable guidance for selecting the most suitable classifier for occupancy detection tasks in IoT environments, ultimately contributing to improved efficiency and effectiveness in IoT-based systems.

articleTitle: AI-Based Suicide Risk Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Suicide is one of the main causes of death worldwide and despite the fact that prevention strategies being applied, the rate of suicide has not changed substantially over the past decades. Suicide risk has proven extremely difficult to assess for medical specialists, and traditional methodologies deployed have not been effective. Advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) make it possible to attempt to predict suicide with the analysis of relevant data aiming to inform clinical practice and this is the focus of this work. The results indicate that Artificial Intelligence models show promising results for predicting which people are most at risk of committing suicide at the time of referral to a mental health service.

articleTitle: Content Creation for Touristic Portals Using ChatGPT
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Our research presents the development of an innovative web-based application designed to assist hoteliers in creating and managing multilingual content for their tourist accommodations for tourism portals. To address this need, our application leverages the advanced capabilities of OpenAI's ChatGPT for automated content generation and DeepL's API for high-quality translations, integrated within a user-friendly interface. Through an integrated development process, we leveraged the capabilities of combining natural language processing with artificial intelligence to meet the specific needs of the tourism and hospitality industry. Our findings indicate that the application significantly streamlines the content creation and translation process, offering hoteliers a competitive edge in a globally connected marketplace. By automating these tasks, the system not only saves time and resources but also ensures consistency and quality in accommodation listings across different languages. The application's impact is further evidenced by its adaptability to various accommodation types and the potential for enhancing guest satisfaction through improved information accessibility. The benefits of our application are supported by a medium scale evaluation.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Transformer Models in Zero-Shot Text Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Ahstract-Zero-shot text classification leverages pre-trained transformer models to categorize texts without the need for task-specific training. This paper analyzes a variety of transformer-based pre-trained methods on the task of zero-shot text classi-fication. Specifically, we present a deep comparative analysis of various transformer models, such as BART, DeBerta, DistiIBART, RoBERTa, and their variants, and evaluate their performance in various zero-shot text classification schemes. Furthermore, we examine the models' generalization capabilities. The findings highlight key strengths and weaknesses of each model, providing insights into their suitability for different text categorization tasks. Our research contributes to the broader understanding of transformer-based approaches and offers guidance for selecting models for zero-shot text classification.

articleTitle: People Counting in Airports for COVID-19 Spreading Prevention using a Simple Computer Vision Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: COVID-19 is an airborne disease that is particularly easy to be spread in indoor places. This is the case since people tend to get crowded and safety distances are not kept. Airports pose a major source of disease spreading since people from different places come together and reside in common places constituting them overcrowded at cases. Especially when people reside or queue up to certain places, (e.g. toilets, restaurants) the risk factor of getting the virus is high. Hence people occupancy, as well as queuing, need to get monitored to inform the passengers about the number of people that occupy a common place. To this end we propose a simple algorithm based on the Yolo8 for people detection, the DeepOCSort algorithm for tracking the people and our simple algorithm for counting the people. Video experiments showed that the algorithm can successfully fulfill the task of counting people.

articleTitle: An Innovative Information System for Supporting Management and AR Visits in Cultural Tourism Points of Interest
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative information system designed to support the management and augmented reality (AR) visits of cultural tourism points of interest, focusing on the fortifications of Aitoloakarnania, Greece. The system integrates advanced technologies including photogrammetry, 3D modeling, virtual reality (VR), AR, and 360° virtual tours to enhance the accessibility and promotion of cultural heritage sites. We describe the technical approaches used to capture, process, and optimize 3D models and panoramic imagery for use in mobile AR and VR applications. The resulting applications provide engaging, interactive experiences for visitors while also serving as management tools for cultural heritage professionals. User evaluation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the system in enhancing cultural tourism experiences. This work showcases how intelligent digital systems can be leveraged to preserve, study, and disseminate cultural content in novel ways, contributing to the field of digital humanities.

articleTitle: A Neural Network-Based Context Handling Mechanism for Accessing the Medical Information of Patients Suffering from Coronary Heart Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: In this time and age, there has been a rise in heart disease risk attributed to contemporary lifestyles, with coronary heart disease being a prevalent concern. Several risk factors contribute to the development of heart disease, such as high cholesterol, high blood pressure, smoking, diabetes, obesity, unhealthy diet, excessive alcohol consumption, and family history of heart disease. Today, artificial intelligence plays a pivotal role in aiding medical professionals in diagnosing such a life-threatening condition. This study focuses on analyzing patients' health metrics to identify if they are suffering from coronary heart disease or not by exploiting machine learning techniques. Specifically, we devised an algorithm employing Deep Neural Networks in combination with Principal Component Analysis for the data preprocessing phase, to predict potential health issues related to coronary heart diseases. Ultimately, this diagnostic context handler which is relied on Neural-Networks combined with Principal Component Analysis preprocessing method is integrated into our patient's health data system for controlling who is able or not to access the patient's sensitive medical information in emergency situations.

articleTitle: Towards an Automated Cultural Heritage Data Processing and Publishing Pipeline
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: We present the automations, tools and techniques we developed in order to streamline the processing, authoring and publication of 3D Models merged with 360 Virtual Tours, which are the outcome of Photogrammetry and 360 Panoramic Photography respectively and are accessible from mobile, Desktop and Virtual Reality Headsets.

articleTitle: Transforming Competence Frameworks into Practice: A Methodological Guide to Online Course Development for Educator Competence Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: This paper presents a methodology for transforming competence frameworks into specific online courses by following a structured approach composed of well-defined steps. The study details the process of translating a set of competences into specific learning outcomes, which form the foundation of the course instructional design. The subsequent development process includes aligning these outcomes with instructional strategies, selecting appropriate teaching methods, and designing assessment tools to measure learner achievement. The methodology emphasizes active stakeholder collaboration, leveraging digital tools to facilitate communication, resource sharing, and continuous feedback. Additionally, it incorporates the ADDIE and Agile methodologies for designing and developing digital course content, outlining specific steps and tools for their implementation. This methodology has been previously implemented and refined based on practical experiences and feedback. In this paper we outline a revised version that has been used in the SPICE online course design, which focuses on developing inclusive STEAM competences for teachers. The implications of this paper highlight the potential for using structured methodologies to effectively translate competence frameworks into practical, impactful online courses for educator development.

articleTitle: Integration of Security in the DevOps Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: This paper investigates the transition to DevSecOps, where the security component is of paramount importance. As digital threats become increasingly sophisticated, the need for security to be embedded within the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) and the Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipelines is imperative. With this emphasis on security integration the produced application and its underlining infrastructure are much more resilient to bugs and vulnerabilities. The findings highlight the shift towards shared security responsibility, the strategic implementation of security tools, and the adoption of security-focused practices from the inception of development.

articleTitle: Image Fusion and Quantum Machine Learning for Remote Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: The integration of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and optical imagery through image fusion techniques is important in refining the accuracy and interpretability of images in remote sensing applications. The current array of available image fusion methods presents a complex landscape, each with its own set of advantages and limitations. This survey paper describes existing image fusion methods, with a primary focus on SAR and optical image classification. This will provide valuable insights for enhanced decision-making in remote sensing applications. In addition to examining image fusion methods, we also study various machine learning algorithms that can be used to classify the data. Although the emphasis is on SAR and optical image fusion, the study will also include a broader discussion of other applications, of image fusion methods across various domains.

articleTitle: Towards Innovative Power-to-Gas Investments in Greece: Novel Simulation Scenarios and Assessment Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Hydrogen and methane, when produced via water electrolysis with the usage of electricity from renewable energy sources (RES), could be used to help decarbonize sectors of the economy where other alternatives are either unfeasible to apply, or more expensive. Given Greece's favorable potential with respect to RES, such as wind and solar power, said power-to-gas (PtG) renewable products are considered crucial in the country's effort to meet its national environmental and energy policy targets. Meanwhile, they are also in accordance with the country's commitment to the EU's broader 2030 and 2050 climate and energy targets in plans such as the Green Deal. The present study proposes several key scenarios involving variants of PtG investments for the case of the Greek energy system, examining the coupling potential with both the natural gas and electricity transmission systems. The analysis emphasizes on setting up the basis for realistic mathematical simulations and their latter accurate techno-economic investigation and optimization, while indicative key performance indicators are identified towards the consistent evaluation and benchmarking of the different investments in question.

articleTitle: “Transforming” Electricity Demand Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: For countries and Energy Power Utilities around the world, accurate and timely forecasting of electricity demand is critical not only for cost-efficient production planning, but also to ensure the stability of the power grid so that everyone has access to electricity for everyone at all times. Using data from Independent Power Transmission Operators (IPTOs), we conduct a lab report that deals with univariate and multivariate electricity time series forecasting. Forecasting time series data is an important part of the time series modeling sector and occupies an important place in the field of energy modeling. The objectives of this paper are to study and train the cutting-edge technology of Transformer Neural Networks for time series forecasting of electricity demand, compare it with other major machine learning technologies and especially the attention-based technologies in this direction, and draw conclusions about the nature and characteristics of Big Energy Data after applying exploratory data analysis. The following text also includes a report describing the elements and characteristics of electricity markets, a literature review of cutting-edge technologies for forecasting energy time series, a description of the Transformer architecture and its application to time series modeling. Finally, we address our thoughts on why our architecture may or may not outperform other electricity demand techniques and discuss future work for another transformer architecture problem in energy modeling.

articleTitle: Spotlighting the Significance of the SRI Methodological Tailoring at Country Level: A Case Study in Greece
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: In addressing the challenges posed by climate change, energy poverty, and energy crises, there is an increasing focus on transitioning to green and fossil fuel-free alternatives, reflecting a strong commitment to sustainable development. The Smart Readiness Indicator, introduced by the European Union, aims to improve the energy efficiency of buildings, adjust operations to meet occupants' needs, and respond to signals from the electricity grid. Consequently, developing new methods for decarbonising the energy system has become essential to meet the energy demands of industries, businesses, transportation, and residential sectors. This necessitates a comprehensive understanding of the situation and the implementation of various actions to reform the regulatory framework, promote technological advancements, stimulate economic growth, and foster collective social efforts. This study focuses on customising the Smart Readiness Indicator methodological framework by adjusting the weighting factors of different domains based on the “energy balance” method. Currently, the European Commission provides standard domain weighting values, however this study is focused on their tailoring in order to reflect specific climate zones. Utilising open data and consumption patterns, the customised weightings are applied to a typical Greek single-family house to demonstrate the differences and underscore the importance of tailored assessments for extracting more accurate results compared to the “standard” methodology. The findings highlight significant improvements, especially in energy efficiency and occupant comfort functionalities, suggesting that tailored approaches can enhance the accuracy of SRI assessments.

articleTitle: Improving Active Face Recognition using Multi-Task Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach leveraging active perception and multi-task learning to enhance face recognition in robotics, particularly addressing occlusions. We trained a Deep Neural Network (DNN) enabling robots to adapt to occlusions by dynamically reposition for optimal facial image capture without prior environmental knowledge while using depth estimation as an auxiliary task. Utilizing simulated environments for algorithm development and testing, our approach significantly improves face recognition accuracy by adjusting the robot's viewing points in response to obstacles. Our experimental evaluation within these simulations demonstrated remarkable improvements: starting from a baseline mean verification score of 70.83% for occluded faces, our method achieved a significant increase to 94.87%. This enhancement illustrates the proposed method's capability to actively navigate and adjust for clearer image acquisition.

articleTitle: Machine-Learning Modelling of a Fluid Flow in a Two-Dimensional Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Over the past decade, the integration of Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) has garnered significant interest, capitalizing on their ability to discern intricate patterns within data. Focused on enhancing computational efficiency, this article explores the application of ANNs in fluid-dynamics simulations, particularly in modelling a benchmark problem of fluid flow in a two-dimensional (2D) channel. Leveraging a Multilayer Perceptron trained on Finite Volume Method numerical data, for both interpolation and extrapolation estimations and various grid resolutions, our findings demonstrate the ANN's prowess as a swift and accurate surrogate for traditional numerical methods. Overall, the results of this work mark a pioneering step towards leveraging Machine Learning for modelling complex relationships in fluids phenomena, promising transformative advancements in Computational Fluid Dynamics.

articleTitle: Medical Decision Support System in Nuclear Medicine Diagnosis for Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer and Coronary Artery Disease: A First Stage Prototype
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the most common form of lung cancer. It is a complex disease typically diagnosed in advanced stages, mainly using image data from PET/CT imaging. Moreover, Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) is the most common type of cardiovascular disease, accounting for almost 33% of total global deaths, and it is commonly diagnosed using multiple methods, such as Myocardial Perfusion Imaging. The work builds on previous research on automated diagnosis based on Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Deep Fuzzy Cognitive Map (DeepFCM) methods. It encapsulates all proposed models into a single holistic tool. This tool, functioning as a Medical Decision Support System (MDSS), offers medical experts practical choices for diagnosing malignant Solitary Pulmonary Nodules (SPN) related to NSCLC or an indication of CAD pathology for a patient. Its holistic approach offers versatility depending on available information and the desired Artificial Intelligence (AI) model for each case. Moreover, breaking the boundaries of common black-box AI models offers an added layer of explainability for each classification result. Thus, this approach can enhance trust and confidence in the model's results and enable users to better understand the decision-making process.

articleTitle: Model Checking with Large Language Models - Initial Experiments and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Large Language Models such as ChatGPT have risen in prominence recently leading to the need to analyse their strengths and limitations on various tasks. The objective of this work is to evaluate the performance of Large Language Models on Model Checking which is used extensively in various critical tasks such as software and hardware verification.

articleTitle: Multi-Criteria Building Performance Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: One of the sustainability goals in Europe is to reduce GHG emissions and energy consumption in buildings by 2030 and achieve climate neutrality by 2050. Renovation targets include a 16% reduction in primary energy use by 2030 in residential buildings and renovating 16% of least efficient buildings in the non-residential sector. Performance indicators in smart buildings are crucial for evaluating system performance objectively, aiding decision-making, and ensuring accountability. They provide insights into energy consumption, indoor air quality, and resource usage, facilitating cost reduction and enhancing user experience. These indicators also support compliance with regulations, certification standards, and sustainability goals. This work, under the umbrella of the DigiBUILD project, applies multi-dimension key performance indicators across ten European pilots to make better-informed decisions, improve data quality, and support policy-making for sustainable building infrastructure.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Spectrum Sensing Capabilities for Future Networks Beyond 5G
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: The wide spread of wireless devices and services has significantly increased the demand for radio spectrum. This leads to congestion, especially in urban areas where many users and devices compete for the same radio frequency bandwidths. Improving the efficiency of spectrum allocation through new technologies and AI algorithms to better optimize radio resource allocation for increased scalability and improved performance is crucial. This paper presents the design and development of an AI framework for spectrum sensing that can be applied to B5G technologies. From the obtained results, we can conclude that the developed AI algorithm ensures a high level of performance achieving an accuracy of 97,1% when classifying 4G and NR 5G communications.

articleTitle: Assessing the Impact of Circular Economy Projects: The DEFINITE-CCRI Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: This paper presents the technical and impact potential assessment provided for selected circular economy projects by DEFINITE-CCRI. Among the main goals of the methodology employed in the DEFINITE-CCRI project are the support of the selected projects enabling them to become more attractive to investors and gain funding and the overall bridging of the gap between the circularity-based innovation and the financing available for its development. The DEFINITE-CCRI impact assessment methodology has been developed based on the 9R strategies, according to which specific indicators have been chosen and tailored to fit the particularities of the projects under assessment and to shed light on their environmental, social, and macro-economic impacts.

articleTitle: KEENsight: Cloud Based Collaborative Environment for Streamlining Machine Learning Development
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Machine learning has transitioned from an individualistic approach to a collaborative one, enabling the collective effort to address increasingly complex challenges as they arise. One challenge that emerges is the management of a collaborative development process in machine learning projects. This paper outlines a collaborative environment KEENsight that leverages the benefits of a collaborative approach by orchestrating various open source tools. It establishes an optimal setting for code collaboration, model generation, data sharing, and the utilization of computational resources not limited to a single location. Through the integrating of these tools, KEENsight aims to streamline the development process and enhance productivity in machine learning.

articleTitle: Enhancing Efficiency and Quality of Services in the Public Service Sector of a Smart City, Through State Fuzzy Cognitive Maps
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: The public service sector plays a crucial role in delivering efficient and high-quality services to citizens. In order to meet the increasing demands and expectations, it is imperative to explore innovative approaches for improving service efficiency and quality. This paper presents a novel framework that combines State Fuzzy Cognitive Maps (FCMs) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques to optimize service delivery in the public service sector. Drawing on inputs such as the number of applications per employee, the regulatory environment, employee competence and the budget allocation, the proposed framework captures the key factors influencing service efficiency and quality. By employing State FCMs, the complex relationships and interdependencies among these factors are modeled and analyzed, providing a comprehensive understanding of the system's behavior. The integration of AI techniques further empowers the framework by enabling data-driven decision-making and optimization processes. Through simulation and optimization algorithms, the system's performance is evaluated and strategies are devised to enhance service efficiency and quality. The outputs of the framework are focused on improved and higher levels of service quality, addressing factors such as budget allocation, process optimization, service responsiveness and accuracy. The paper discusses real-world case studies and practical implementations of the proposed framework in the public service sector. It highlights the benefits of this approach, including enhanced employee competence, streamlined operations, personalized service delivery, and increased citizen satisfaction. Moreover, it emphasizes the importance of continuous evaluation and refinement to ensure the sustained improvement of service efficiency and quality.

articleTitle: Smart Garbage Separators: A Comparative Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: When we want machines to perform tedious and dangerous tasks for us, it becomes necessary to prepare them to efficiently emulate our smart thinking and learning. For instance, when a garbage separator has to separate different categories of material like human learning does, there is a need to make them to explore an innovative application of reinforcement learning (RL) to improve the efficiency and accuracy of separation and selection. But before to start the process it is very important to perform a comparative study on existing methodologies [1]–[50] by avoiding duplication of existing work. Thus, in this paper we perform a comparative study on a large number of recent methods and we provide our overall evaluation. Then we proceed with one extra step by improving a low performing methodology to elevate its performance by showing to our team the collaborative work for better results. Thus, it is crucial for effective waste management to leverage RL algorithms to optimize the sorting process in real-time, adapting dynamically to changes in the waste stream. By integrating sensors and AI techniques the smart garbage separator behaves as an autonomous agent within its operational environment, making decisions to classify and direct waste into appropriate categories such as recyclables, organics, and landfill. The RL model employs a reward-based system where actions—defined as sorting decisions—are continuously refined based on feedback regarding sorting accuracy and processing speed. Using a combination of real-world data collection and simulated environments, we implement and compare traditional Q-learning and Deep Q-Network (DQN) algorithms to determine their efficacy in handling complex, high-dimensional state spaces typical of waste material characteristics. The results indicate significant improvements in sorting accuracy and operational efficiency, showcasing the potential of RL to transform waste management practices.

articleTitle: Virtual-GymVR: A Virtual Reality Platform for Personalized Exergames
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Virtual-Gym<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">VR</sup> is a platform for serious exergames in virtual reality. Its purpose is to provide older adults with a fun experience, while, at the same time, encouraging them to complete their personalized exercise sessions. The platform takes as input a description of a prescribed exercise, in terms of a posture-transition grammar, and constructs personalized versions of its games by configuring the behavior of the interactive objects in these games accordingly. The game-configuration process essentially controls the placement and the interaction behavior of the games' objects so that they induce the user to adopt the proper postures, as described by the input exercise specification. At run time, the sequence of game events stimulates the user to move to the prescribed exercise postures and, thus, accomplish their own personalized exercise goals. Given the intended user population of older adults, we have designed three different Virtual <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text { -Gym }{ }^{\text{VR}}$</tex> games with metaphors appropriate for three different types of exercises. Our initial experimentation with the Virtual <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-\text{Gym}^{\text{VR}}$</tex> games indicates that the approach is promising.

articleTitle: An Approach to Associate Provenance From ML Pipelines With Transparency and Accountability
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: The data growth has raised predictive models in order to enhance data-driven decision-making. One challenge underlying such tasks regards the extent to which these artificial intelligence models can be trusted. Trustworthiness in Artificial Intelligence (AI) encompasses properties, such as fairness, robustness, accountability, explainability, and transparency, which are pillars for reliable AI systems development. To help matters, recent research highlights the importance of provenance to AI Trust in Machine Learning (ML) pipelines. In this light, this work proposes an approach to associate provenance from ML pipelines with Transparency and Accountability, considering a measurable way to promote more confidence in ML models. Key contributions include defining metrics for integrating provenance with Transparency and Accountability based on extracting and documenting new metadata obtained through a given ML pipeline. In order to evaluate the proposed approach, a prototype has been developed and some experiments have been accomplished.

articleTitle: A Survey on Algorithms and Software for the Frequent Itemset Hiding Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Privacy preserving data mining is an increasingly popular field of research with many problems being actively researched in this domain. Specifically, the Frequent Itemset Hiding Problem (FIHP) poses significant challenges in data mining, particularly concerning the privacy-preserving extraction of frequent itemsets from sensitive datasets. This survey paper comprehensively explores the landscape of software solutions dedicated to addressing the FIHP. Through an extensive review of existing methodologies, algorithms, and implementations, this survey provides a systematic analysis of the state-of-the-art in FIHP software. The survey categorizes and evaluates various approaches, ranging from traditional Apriori-based algorithms to recent advancements leveraging graph-based techniques and machine learning. By synthesizing the existing literature and high-lighting emerging trends, this survey aims to guide researchers and practitioners in selecting suitable software solutions for tackling the FIHP in diverse data mining applications.

articleTitle: Mathematics Anxiety and the Mozart Effect. A Comparative Study on Emotional Intelligence in Mathematics E-Learning Among Music and General Education Students
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Addressing mathematics anxiety using techniques from affective computing, including emotion recognition and generation, and incorporating theories like the Mozart effect, can potentially improve student outcomes by mitigating negative emotional responses related to math learning. To investigate possible relation of mathematics anxiety with the Mozart effect, this study explores the relationship between emotional intelligence, attitudes toward mathematics, and academic performance among high school students attending music and general schools. The objectives of the research are twofold: first, to understand how emotional intelligence influences attitudes toward mathematics, and second, to investigate the impact of attitudes toward mathematics on students' academic performance. A sample of 182 high school students from both types of schools was used to explore the associations between emotional intelligence, attitudes toward mathematics, and overall grades in mathematics. The short form of Attitudes Toward Mathematics Inventory (ATMI) and Emotional Intelligence Assessment (EIA) were utilized to gather data on students' attitudes and emotional intelligence levels, respectively. Statistical analyses used to examine the research questions. The findings revealed a significant correlation between emotional intelligence and attitudes toward mathematics, suggesting that students with higher emotional intelligence exhibited more favorable attitudes toward the subject. Additionally, a notable distinction emerges in emotional intelligence levels between students from music schools and general schools, with the former group demonstrating higher emotional intelligence scores. However, attitudes toward mathematics remained similar across both school types. Educators can use this information to create strategies to support students' overall growth, linking educational settings with emotional intelligence to enhance cognitive and emotional learning.

articleTitle: AI in Smart Tourism: LLMs & GPTs Leading the Way
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: The rise of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has dramatically transformed various industries, including healthcare, finance, education, and transportation, with Large Language Models (LLMs) playing a pivotal role in this evolution. In the realm of Smart Tourism, LLMs, including Generative Pre-trained Transformers (GPTs), have demonstrated significant potential, providing innovative solutions to enhance tourist experiences and streamline industry operations. This paper provides an overview of the LLMs currently available in the market, with a specific focus on the GPT models in the context of Smart Tourism. It examines their performance, datasets, and potential applications within this sector. The study analyzes the data utilized by these models and their interaction with travelers, emphasizing the need for diverse training data to enhance the cultural and contextual relevance of GPT responses. This concise study offers a comprehensive understanding of the transformative potential of LLMs and GPTs in Smart Tourism, providing valuable insights for researchers and industry professionals and serving as a stepping stone for further research in the field.

articleTitle: A Decision Support Tool for Aggregation and Prioritisation of Energy Efficiency Investments in Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Reducing buildings' energy consumption through energy efficiency interventions has become a key priority to mitigate climate change. To this end, stakeholders involved in the implementation and financing of energy efficiency projects in the building sector could benefit from the development of specific methodologies and user-friendly tools that can assist them by supporting them in managing large datasets and by simplifying decision making processes. In this context, the aim of this paper is to propose a decision-making tool for triggering investments in energy efficiency. The tool's workflow consists of three layers: project selection (layer 1) - narrowing down the list of potential energy efficiency projects according to investor preferences, aggregation (layer 2) - leveraging an optimisation algorithm to create clusters of similar projects, and finally, prioritisation (layer 3) - applying the TOPSIS (Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution) method to rank the clusters. The tool brings significant added value to stakeholders involved in financing energy efficiency interventions, offering standardisation and automation of procedures.

articleTitle: A Holistic Framework for Evaluating Energy Performance and Indoor Environmental Quality in Cultural Heritage Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: The New European Bauhaus movement advocates a holistic approach to architecture that emphasizes the integration of design, technology, and social responsibility. Historic buildings embody cultural heritage and architectural significance, presenting a unique challenge to retrofit them to meet modern indoor environmental quality (IEQ) standards and energy efficiency requirements without compromising their integrity. Towards this challenge, the present paper introduces an assessment framework that considers both the preservation of historic character and the adoption of innovative strategies for energy efficiency and IEQ improvement. The framework utilizes a wide range of criteria, including indicators that monitor energy intensity, smart readiness, thermal comfort, air quality, as well as visual and acoustic comfort. By measuring such indicators, stakeholders can evaluate the current status of cultural heritage buildings, identify areas for improvement, and quantify the effectiveness of retrofit interventions. In conclusion, the paper highlights the importance of developing tailored IEQ and energy efficiency assessment tools for historic buildings that reflect both their cultural significance and their potential to contribute to a more sustainable built environment.

articleTitle: eXtended Reality Services for Outdoor Cultural Spaces: System Design and Evaluation Framework Using Unbiased Biometric Data
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: The concept of enriching the visible reality with more information has led to the development of the eXtended Reality technology, where digital elements like text, images, 3D representations and virtual scenarios, are embedded to the real world and become visible to humans via mobile devices. Cultural Heritage is embracing eXtended Reality and tries to find new ways to harvest its merits in an endless struggle to disseminate cultural information to the public and the next generations. In this paper, we are presenting an innovative intelligent Environment, operating in outdoor cultural spaces and offering personalized eXtended Reality cultural experiences to visitors. The Environment aims to support the financial sustainability of cultural heritage institutes by attracting visitors and especially younger ones, as well as create new sources of revenue for cultural heritage professionals by allowing them to create XR experiences, without the help of IT professionals and exploiting them in an online market of XR cultural experiences. We propose a novel framework to evaluate the user experience by collecting biometric data (brain activity and eye behavior) from the visitors of outdoor cultural spaces and exploring their cognition and emotions while using the new Environment.

articleTitle: Investigating the Agreement with Human Readers and Generalisation Capabilities of a Transfer Learning Approach for Predicting the Malignancy of Solitary Pulmonary Nodules in CT Screening
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Lung cancer remains a leading global health issue. This research used artificial intelligence to enhance lung nodule characterisation within CT screening. Using transfer learning techniques, the study emphasised the concordance between AI predictions and human-assigned labels. Leveraging a pre-trained VGG19 model, two independent datasets of lung nodule images were investigated. Overall, high agreement and classification performance were seen in the training dataset. However, a drop in model reliability on unseen data was noted, highlighting the challenges of perfect agreement between AI and human interpretations. Still, high sensitivity, TPR, and AUC values affirmed the efficacy of the paradigm chosen. Despite areas of potential improvement, the approach demonstrated the promising role AI and transfer learning could play in early lung cancer detection. Future improvements in AI interpretability may yield even more robust, clinically viable prediction models.

articleTitle: Identity and Digital Self-Representation in the Metaverse
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Rapid digitization, the impact of social media and the phenomenal growth of the Metaverse has met with both positive and negative responses. Along with optimism about the possibilities and efficiencies created via AI, there have also been concerns. Many fields are now using the Metaverse in commercial applications, leading to new ways of increasing revenues and enhancing sustainability. Central to this concept are avatars, which serve as digital embodiments of users, facilitating interactions and the representation of self within this virtual environment. This paper underscores the profound implications of virtual identity, combined with the psychological and sociocultural dimensions of avatar selection, highlighting the complex motivations behind avatar customization. The potential for avatars to influence user behavior, facilitate escapism, and impact psychological well-being is significant, and this emphasizes the need for ethical considerations and protective measures for users navigating these virtual spaces. This paper is about the potentials and pitfalls regarding the use of avatars as digital representations of people, and the impact of such developments on an individual's personal identity conceptions.

articleTitle: Developing an Anti -Phishing Large Language Model: A Focus Group Study on Human, Technological, and Legal Factors
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: The phishing problem poses a significant threat in modern information systems, putting both individuals and businesses at risk of financial and professional harm. Owing to social media's rapid development and widespread appeal, deception of this sort is hurting millions of people and growing more dangerous. The current work, as part of the AILA (Artificial Intelligence-driven Framework and Legal Advice Tools for Phishing Prevention and Mitigation in Information Systems) project, aims to specify and validate an AI-driven multifactor (human, technology and legal) anti-phishing data model, with the implementation of focus group studies. The findings assist to provide human, technology, and legislative user model endpoints that will be identified and discussed for explicit and implicit user modeling, which will guide the development of the corresponding AI-driven user modeling and profiling mechanisms. To this end a Large Language System is planned to be employed.

articleTitle: Methodology for Assuring Interoperability in Demand-Response Services
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Building Energy Management Systems (BEMS) have become very popular in the last decade. Many vendors and integrators are providing their own solutions to be deployed in buildings, which sometimes co-exist in the same building. The variety of protocols and communication mechanisms included in these solutions should be considered. Hence, interoperability plays a crucial role in ensuring that these systems can provide a holistic energy management strategy and integrate monitoring and control elements. This work presents a framework to allow the information exchange between sensors, controllers and software services aiming to ensure interoperability in demand response strategies. Under this approach, an interoperable architecture is defined where the core element is the data model to represent information. In this sense, domOS Common Ontology is selected as the kernel and some extensions have been done in order to better include the representation of building assets, Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and user profiles and preferences. Besides, other extensions have been used to represent other devices and units of measurement.

articleTitle: Recent Advancements in Search-Engine Algorithms for Efficiency, Privacy and Security
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: This survey explores the technical aspects of how companies implement their search engines to minimize costs. In addition, by examining the algorithms and techniques employed by various companies, the current paper seeks to understand the strategies used for analyzing data and delivering personalized results, while preserving the user's privacy. In particular, the study scrutinizes specific algorithmic choices, architectures, efficiency, security measures, and vulnerabilities. It identifies nuances in search result personalization and evaluates diverse algorithms to discern best practices in search engine optimization. Additionally, the paper investigates how emerging AI and machine learning technologies can innovate current search engine capabilities. Through the aforementioned theoretical analysis, the current survey aims to highlight what renders these systems efficient, secure, or susceptible to potential vulnerabilities, thus, laying the groundwork for future research on the development of robust and resilient search-engine architectures.

articleTitle: Evolutionary and Quantum Computing for Community Detection: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Information, Intelligence, Systems & Applications (IISA)
abstract: Rising quantum technologies undertake to provide new strategies for solving hard combinatorial problems. Community detection is a fundamental issue in network studies with applications in various complex systems.
